record.what_it_does: Time tracking, invoicing, expenses and project management SaaS with a public REST API v2.
record.auth_notes: OAuth2 authorization code (and implicit) via Harvest ID; personal access tokens for own scripts. Requests also need a Harvest-Account-Id header.
record.access_notes: Anyone with a Harvest ID can create PATs and OAuth2 apps at id.getharvest.com/developers. The docs describe no app review. Using the API needs a Harvest account, which has a free tier, though I didn't check its limits.
record.api_breadth_notes: Covers clients, contacts, invoices, estimates, expenses, tasks, time entries, projects, users, roles, reports, PTO, approvals, notifications, reimbursements, imports and Forecast. This is well over 50 operations.
record.mcp_notes: Harvest's help center article "Harvest MCP" gives the endpoint https://api.harvestapp.com/mcp. I only saw this in search results, because the article returned 403 when fetched. Community servers also exist, such as ianaleck/harvest-mcp-server.
record.blocker_notes: No blocker found. The docs describe no OAuth app review, and the PAT and OAuth2 app creation pages are self-serve.

evidence.quote: Personal Access Tokens are the preferred method when you want to write your own scripts that consume our API.
The V2 API requires an access token to authenticate requests.
Clients API, Invoices API, Estimates API, Expenses API, Timesheets API, Projects API, Reports API, Forecast API

record.needs_human: Check whether the Harvest API v2 offers webhooks. I didn't find any mention in the docs index. Check whether a sandbox or test account exists. Open the Harvest MCP help article, which returned 403 to me, to confirm the endpoint and its auth. Confirm the free plan's API limits.
